card.h1: Project Meridian: handover pack for the incoming owner
This is a fictional worked example
card.p: Kestrel Data, Project Meridian, and every name, figure, contract and date in this pack are invented to demonstrate what a complete handover looks like. Nothing here describes a real company or real results.

ul.li: Company: Kestrel Data, B2B workforce analytics, 310 staff, 1,180 customers
Project: replacing the homegrown billing system with vendor platform Nomad Billing
Pack written: 23 September 2026, by Priya Raghunathan, outgoing owner

card.p: Figures marked assumption in this pack are illustrative planning inputs, not measurements. Everything else is presented as the project's own recorded numbers.

card.h1: Where Meridian stands today, in one page

ul.li: Overall: amber. Delivery is on track; budget and one dependency are not.
Phase 1 (catalog, invoicing, payments): live since 4 May 2026. All new business has been written on Nomad since that date.
Phase 2 (account migration): 707 of 1,140 eligible accounts moved, 62% complete. Eight waves left, ending 14 January 2027.
Phase 3 (revenue recognition, dunning): not started, target 26 February 2027
Budget: $2.4M approved, $1.52M spent, $2.61M forecast — 8.75% over, approval pending
Biggest single risk: 88 complex accounts nobody has migrated a pattern for yet

card.h1: How this pack runs

ol.li: Context and scope — why the project exists, what it covers, what it deliberately does not
Where things stand — status by workstream, migration numbers, budget, quality
How it runs — cadence, systems, access, the runbook, the vendor
People and decisions — owners, settled decisions, open ones, risks, dependencies
Your first 90 days — sequenced actions, open questions, handover terms

card.h1: Context and scope
Billing was the constraint on every pricing decision Kestrel wanted to make
card.p: The homegrown system, BillingSvc, was written in 2017 for a single annual seat-based plan sold in USD.

ul.li: Pricing was frozen: usage-based and hybrid plans needed engineering work per contract; Sales had 41 bespoke arrangements maintained by hand
Close took too long: Finance spent 9 of 10 close days reconciling invoices in spreadsheets
Errors were visible to customers: 4.8% of invoices needed a manual correction in June 2026
Nobody owned it: two part-time engineers, no roadmap, no test coverage on proration

card.p: The board approved Meridian in December 2025 on a three-year payback. That payback was an assumption built from the 2025 cost base, not a measured result.

card.h1: What Meridian covers

ul.li: Subscription catalog — plans, add-ons, ramps, discounts, all configurable without a deploy
Invoicing and payments — generation, delivery, card and ACH collection, credit notes
Tax — calculation and filing data via Tessera Tax across 34 jurisdictions
Dunning — automated retry and escalation ladder for failed payments (Phase 3)
Revenue recognition — ASC 606 schedules generated from contract terms (Phase 3)
Self-serve checkout — the public purchase flow, re-pointed to Nomad

Account migration — moving the 1,140 eligible accounts and their 4,190 subscriptions off BillingSvc. The customer base is 1,180; the 40 perpetual-licence accounts below are carved out of that total, so every migration figure in this pack is measured against 1,140.

card.h1: What Meridian deliberately does not cover
card.p: Each exclusion was a steering-committee decision, not an oversight. Resist requests to absorb them.

ul.li: Usage metering pipeline — owned by Data Platform; Meridian consumes its API, does not rebuild it
Sales-assisted quoting UI — stays in Salesforce CPQ, owned by Deal Desk
Multi-entity consolidation — deferred to FY28 with the EMEA entity work
Alternative payment methods — no wallets, no crypto, no regional rails beyond SEPA
40 legacy perpetual-licence accounts — run off inside BillingSvc through FY28, never migrated. Subtracting them from 1,180 customers is what gives the 1,140 eligible base.
Commission calculation — remains in the Sales Ops spreadsheet model

card.h1: Three phases, one cutover per wave, sixteen waves in total

ul.li: Phase 0 — Jan to Mar 2026: vendor selection, contract, data model mapping. Complete.
Phase 1 — Apr to May 2026: catalog, invoicing, payments live for new business on 4 May. Complete.
Phase 2 — Jun 2026 to Jan 2027: eligible accounts migrated in fortnightly Thursday waves. Waves 1 to 8 ran 4 June to 10 September; waves 9 to 16 run 8 October to 14 January. In flight.
Phase 3 — Nov 2026 to Feb 2027: revenue recognition and dunning, overlapping the last migration waves. Target 26 February. Not started.
Phase 4 — FY28: BillingSvc decommission. Not funded, date undecided.

card.p: No wave ran on 24 September. The slot was held so the complex-account design could land first.

card.h1: Where things stand
Status by workstream

ul.li: Migration waves — green. 707 of 1,140 eligible accounts live. Wave 9 ships 8 October. Owner: Hannah Blum.
Complex accounts — red. 88 accounts with multi-year ramps or custom terms have no migration pattern. Design due 23 October. Owner: Marcus Oyelaran.
Tax integration — amber. Live in 34 jurisdictions; 19 open EU rounding discrepancies, the same 19 counted in the exception ledger. Owner: Tomás Iriarte.
Revenue recognition — amber. Design signed off, build not started, start date depends on an open decision. Owner: Tomás Iriarte.
Self-serve checkout — green. Live since 4 May; awaiting Growth's pricing test before any redesign.
Legacy run-off — green. BillingSvc frozen, read-only for migrated accounts, two engineers on call.

card.h1: Migration is 62% done and the remainder is the hard part

ul.li: 1,140 eligible accounts, being 1,180 customers less the 40 perpetual-licence exclusions
707 migrated across eight completed waves, 4 June to 10 September, averaging 88 accounts a wave
433 accounts remaining, of which 88 are classed complex
8 waves left, fortnightly on Thursdays from 8 October, about 54 accounts each, ending 14 January 2027
4,190 active subscriptions on the eligible base; migrated accounts carry 2,612 of them
2 of the eight completed waves slipped by a week; none has been rolled back, and there have been no customer-visible billing outages traceable to a wave

card.p: Average wave size drops from 88 to 54 on purpose. The straightforward accounts are nearly exhausted, and wave 15 falls on 31 December — see the risk register before you agree to it.

card.h1: Budget is forecast 8.75% over, driven by one scope change

ul.li: Approved: $2.40M — $1.05M vendor, $0.98M internal delivery, $0.37M contingency
Spent to 31 August: $1.52M (63% of approved)
Forecast at completion: $2.61M, a $210K overrun. The forecast assumes the remaining waves run at planned effort and Phase 3 scopes as designed; neither is yet tested.
Driver: Tessera Tax integration, added April 2026 when Nomad's native tax missed 11 jurisdictions. $164K build, $48K annual licence upsize still unsigned.
Remaining contingency: $60K
Status: a revised funding paper went to the CFO on 11 September; no decision yet. Chase it in week one.

card.h1: Invoice accuracy improved fourfold but has stalled short of target

ul.li: June 2026: 4.8% of invoices required a manual correction
September 2026: 1.3%, against a target of 0.5% by December
Open exception tickets: 31 — 19 EU tax rounding, 7 mid-cycle proration, 5 currency conversion timing
Share of causes: tax rounding 61%, proration 23%, currency timing 16%
What is not working: the last three weeks show no improvement. The proration adapter needs rework, and that work is not scheduled.

card.p: The 19 EU rounding tickets are the same items tracked as a tax-integration workstream issue and as a medium risk. One count, three places.

card.h1: How it runs
The operating cadence

ul.li: Monday 09:30, 15 min — squad standup. Whole delivery team. Blockers only.
Wednesday 14:00, 45 min — wave review. Go/no-go on the next wave, exception triage. Hannah chairs; you approve. The review the day before a wave Thursday is the decisive one.
Alternate Thursday 16:00, 30 min — steering. CFO, CTO, VP RevOps. You present status, budget, and decisions sought. Pack due Wednesday noon.
Monthly, first three business days — close check-in. With the Controller. Non-negotiable; billing blocks the close.
Quarterly — vendor business review. With Nomad's CSM. Next: 14 October.

card.p: Cancel the standup before you cancel the wave review.

card.h1: Where everything lives

ul.li: Runbooks and design docs: Confluence space BILL, index page "Meridian Home"
Work tracking: Jira project MER; migration waves are epics MER-400 to MER-415, one per wave
Production access: IAM group billing-admin; request via Access Portal, approved by the CTO, 24-hour turnaround
Sandbox: nomad-sbx-2, refreshed from production every Sunday
Dashboards: Looker folder "Meridian Ops" — wave burndown, exception rate, cash collected
Incidents: Slack #meridian-oncall, PagerDuty service "Billing Platform"
Contracts and the funding paper: Drive folder "Meridian / Commercial", restricted to the steering group

card.h1: What to do when billing breaks

ol.li: Declare in #meridian-oncall. Page the Billing Platform service. The on-call engineer leads; you handle comms.
Check the wave first. Most incidents so far have followed a migration wave within 72 hours. The rollback script is documented at BILL/runbooks/wave-rollback.
Never edit invoices directly in Nomad. Corrections go through credit note plus reissue, or the audit trail breaks rev-rec.
Escalate to the vendor at P1 within 30 minutes. Their SLA clock starts at the ticket, not the phone call.
Tell Finance before customers. The Controller decides whether an invoice run is held.

card.h1: The vendor relationship, in the terms that matter

ul.li: Vendor: Nomad Billing. CSM Elena Petrova, weekly office hours Thursdays.
Contract: $310K per year, three-year term to 31 March 2029. Renewal notice 90 days — diary 31 December 2028.
Support SLA: P1 two-hour response, P2 one business day. Credits are claimable but must be requested within 30 days; we have never claimed one.
Committed roadmap items: multi-currency payouts Q1 2027, native EU tax expansion unscheduled.
Relationship health: good but transactional. Elena responds to written escalation, not to Slack.

card.h1: People and decisions
Who owns what

ul.li: Dana Whitfield, CFO — sponsor. Funding, scope changes, the year-end call. Decides; does not attend detail.
You — project owner. Delivery, budget, steering pack, all open decisions below.
Marcus Oyelaran, Engineering Lead. Platform build, proration adapter, complex-account patterns. Sole expert on the adapter.
Hannah Blum, RevOps Manager. Wave planning, customer comms, go/no-go recommendation.
Tomás Iriarte, Finance Systems Lead. Tax, revenue recognition, close readiness.
Wei Zhang, QA. Wave regression suite, exception triage.
Sanjay Rao, Data Platform. Metering API — a dependency, not a team member.

card.p: Eleven people total; five engineers report to Marcus, not to you.

card.h1: Five decisions already made — reopen these only with new evidence

ul.li: Buy, not build (Feb 2026). Build was costed at 26 engineer-months against an 18-month deadline.
Waves, not big bang (Mar 2026). Finance would not accept a single cutover across a close period.
Tessera Tax over Nomad native tax (Apr 2026). Nomad covered 23 of our 34 jurisdictions. This is the source of the overrun, and the judgment here is that it was still the right call.
Keep BillingSvc read-only rather than decommission at cutover (May 2026). Audit needs FY26 and FY27 history queryable.
Do not migrate the 40 perpetual-licence accounts (Jul 2026). They run off by FY28; migration cost exceeded remaining revenue. This decision is why the denominator is 1,140 rather than 1,180.

card.h1: Four decisions are waiting for you

ul.li: Revenue recognition before or after year-end close? Phase 2 finishes 14 January, so a pre-close go-live puts rev-rec and the close on Tomás in the same three weeks. After means two months of manual schedules. Sponsor: CFO. Due 6 November.
Who owns dunning policy — Finance or Customer Success? Blocks Phase 3 build; both teams have said "the other one". Due 16 October.
Sign the $48K Tessera licence upsize? Current tier caps at 25,000 calculations a month; we hit 23,100 in August. Due 30 October.
Set a BillingSvc decommission date. Unfunded, unowned, and costing $7K a month in hosting. Needs a date at steering to become real.

card.h1: Risk register

ul.li: Complex-account migration slips — high, likely. 88 accounts, no pattern, design due 23 October. Mitigation: Marcus prototyping three archetypes; fallback is to extend waves into February. Owner: Marcus.
Key-person dependency on the proration adapter — high. Marcus is the only person who understands it. Mitigation: pairing sessions were scheduled and then cancelled twice. Unresolved. Owner: you.

Wave 15 falls on 31 December — medium. Holiday cover is thin and Finance is closed. Moving it pushes the final wave from 14 January to 28 January and into the close. Decide at the 16 December wave review. Owner: Hannah.
EU tax rounding discrepancies — medium. The 19 open tickets, customer-visible in small amounts. Owner: Tomás.
Budget approval refused or trimmed — medium. Would stop the Tessera upsize and cap throughput. Owner: you.
January close contention — medium. Finance capacity is fully committed weeks 1 to 3. Owner: Tomás.
Vendor slips multi-currency payouts — low but contractual. Q1 2027 commitment; APAC expansion depends on it. Owner: you.

card.h1: Four things you depend on and do not control

ul.li: Metering API v3, Data Platform. Due 20 November. Phase 3 usage billing cannot be tested without it. Sanjay Rao has flagged a two-week risk. Check it weekly.
Salesforce CPQ field mapping freeze, Deal Desk. Kira Lund agreed no schema changes until 31 January, which covers the last wave. Unwritten; get it in email.
Tessera Tax commercial approval, Procurement. Two-week cycle once the CFO decision lands.
Growth pricing experiment. Runs to 30 November. Any checkout redesign waits for its result; do not let Growth start earlier.

card.p: Security review of the PCI scope change closed on 12 August — that one is done.

card.h1: Open questions nobody has answered

ul.li: Who owns billing after Meridian closes? There is no permanent operating team. This needs an answer before Phase 3, not after.
What is the actual target for invoice accuracy? 0.5% was chosen in a workshop and never validated against what customers tolerate. Treat it as an assumption, not a commitment.
Do the 41 bespoke arrangements get standardised? Sales has resisted twice. Migrating them as-is embeds them for years.
Is the three-year payback still credible? The original case assumed no tax engine and a FY27 decommission. Neither holds.
Should the 40 perpetual-licence accounts really run off untouched? The carve-out was priced in July 2026 and nobody has rechecked it against the $7K a month BillingSvc hosting cost.

card.h1: Your first ninety days
card.p: Day one is 1 October, so the three blocks run to 30 October, 29 November and 29 December.

ul.li: Days 1–30. Chase the funding decision. Attend the 8 October and 22 October waves without changing anything. Sit in on the 14 October vendor business review while I still chair it. Read the proration adapter design with Marcus and book the pairing sessions properly. Resolve the dunning ownership question by 16 October and sign or refuse the Tessera upsize by 30 October.

Days 31–60. Take the complex-account design to steering with a dated plan, now that 23 October has passed. Land the rev-rec timing decision by 6 November. Get the CPQ freeze in writing. Check the Metering API v3 date with Sanjay before 20 November. Put a named owner against post-project billing operations.

Days 61–90. Settle the 31 December wave at the 16 December review; that call is yours alone. Reforecast the whole programme with Phase 3 scoped properly. Set the decommission date. Get the accuracy target either validated or changed. Book the January vendor business review and chair it yourself.

card.h1: Week one, and how to reach me

ol.li: Request billing-admin access on day one — it takes 24 hours and blocks everything else
Read BILL/Meridian Home end to end — roughly two hours, and it is current to 19 September
Meet Marcus, Hannah and Tomás individually before your first steering
Sit in on the 7 October wave review, the day before wave 9 ships, and say nothing
Chase the funding paper with the CFO's EA, not with the CFO

card.p: Handover terms: I shadow you until 9 October and answer questions until 30 October. After that I am on Data Platform and the escalation path is Marcus, then the CTO.

brief.instruction: Plain, specific, operational — written by a departing owner to their successor, not to a boardroom. Second person where the reader has to act ("chase it in week one"), third person for facts. Flat declaratives, no hedging, no throat-clearing. Target ~65 words per slide; the template holds median 67, p90 106, so budget 65 and go to 100+ only on the register, status, and scope slides where the reader needs the whole list in one place. Every bullet carries a fact, a number, a name, or a date. Where something is unresolved or was done badly, say so plainly — an honest handover is more useful than a tidy one. Keep the three registers distinct in the wording. Recorded project facts are stated flat. Illustrative planning inputs (the three-year payback, the 0.5% accuracy target, the forecast at completion) are named as assumptions in the sentence that carries them. Judgments (that Tessera was still the right call, that the remainder is the hard part) read as the outgoing owner's opinion, not as measurement. Never dress an assumption or an opinion as a recorded number. Structure rules: vary sentence and paragraph length; never the "Bold term: explanation" rhythm for every item in a list — mix labelled items with plain sentences; no signposting like "Let's explore"; no sweeping openers or motivational closers; none of the "not just X — it's Y" contrast family; no em dashes.

This deck is read alone at a desk, so scanability outranks drama. Use the template's data furniture heavily: ruled ledgers for status, owners, decisions and dependencies; the risk register treatment with severity chips for the risks slide; big-number pairs for the migration and budget figures; a horizontal timeline for the phases, marked with the two wave blocks (4 June to 10 September, 8 October to 14 January) and the held 24 September slot; a scored table where options or statuses are compared. Let the dark section dividers mark the five parts. Where a slide shows the 62% figure, show its denominator in the same visual unit: 707 of 1,140 eligible, never 707 alone against 1,180. Keep imagery sparse and documentary, and never decorative on a data slide. At most three or four images across the whole deck: the cover, and the section dividers where a calm operational photograph helps pacing. No stock-looking handshake or teamwork imagery, no people facing camera, no logos or readable text in images. Card 2 must read unmistakably as a disclaimer — treat it as a labelled notice, not a normal content slide. Invented figures must never be styled as audited results: no source lines implying external provenance, and no "source:" footers citing bodies that do not exist.

Every name, figure, date and contract term in this outline is invented for a fictional worked example and must stay internally consistent across slides. The canonical ledger below was calculated, and no slide may contradict it: 1,180 customers total, minus 40 perpetual-licence accounts excluded by the July 2026 decision, gives 1,140 eligible accounts. That 1,140 is the only migration denominator used anywhere. 707 eligible accounts migrated = 62% of 1,140. 433 remain, of which 88 are complex. 707 + 433 = 1,140. Waves are fortnightly on Thursdays. Waves 1 to 8 completed: 4, 18 June; 2, 16, 30 July; 13, 27 August; 10 September 2026 — averaging 88 accounts each. No wave on 24 September. Waves 9 to 16 remain: 8, 22 October; 5, 19 November; 3, 17, 31 December 2026; 14 January 2027 — about 54 accounts each (433 over 8). Phase 2 ends 14 January 2027, not February. Sixteen waves in total. 4,190 active subscriptions on the eligible base; migrated accounts carry 2,612. Exceptions: 31 open tickets = 19 EU tax rounding (61%), 7 proration (23%), 5 currency timing (16%). Nineteen is the canonical EU rounding count on every slide that mentions it; there is no separate count of nine. Budget: $2.40M approved, $1.52M spent to 31 August, $2.61M forecast, $210K overrun, 8.75% over, $60K contingency left. Quality: 4.8% correction rate in June 2026, 1.3% in September, 0.5% target. Do not change a number in one place without changing it everywhere. Do not add new statistics, vendors, people or dates beyond those given, and do not soften the items the outline marks as unresolved.
